cut_items.item: Alternative: merge target branch into feature branch to avoid force push (adds a merge commit)
If a teammate has the branch checked out, they should run git reset --hard origin/branch; a plain git pull would merge old and new history together
Open pull request is updated by the push; review comments on old commits may become outdated
Command git log HEAD..origin/branch to see unknown remote commits (note: Y's command direction is more precise)
Teammates should use git reset --hard origin/branch after the push; a normal git pull would merge old and new history together (explicit warning)
If branch has an open pull request, force push updates it, and review comments on old commits may become outdated
Alternative: merge the target branch into the feature branch instead of rebasing, which pushes without force but adds a merge commit
Do not force-push main, master, or any shared branch (X mentions main/develop, so overlap)

added_items.item: Troubleshooting: if --force-with-lease is rejected with stale info, fetch, inspect new remote commits, rebase onto them, and retry
Force push permanently replaces remote history; commits only on the remote are lost unless someone has a local copy
Explicit explanation that the rejection is due to non-fast-forward because commits have new hashes
Uses git log --oneline origin/<branch> ^<branch> to list remote-only commits, which correctly shows what would be overwritten
Explanation that the rebase gives commits new hashes so push can't fast-forward (Y also says history rewritten, so mostly overlap)
Command to list remote commits not in local branch: git log origin/<branch> ^<branch> after fetch (Y gives HEAD..origin/branch, equivalent)
Warning that force push permanently replaces remote history and commits only on the remote are lost unless someone has a local copy
Teammates should tell/notify others first, then fetch and rebase onto origin/<branch> or reset
Troubleshooting: if --force-with-lease is rejected with 'stale info', fetch, inspect new remote commits, rebase onto them, retry
